summary: Jan Fontein worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earning his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin. He served as a curator at the Rijksmuseum and was curator of Asiatic art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Jan Gonda was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies who completed his PhD at Utrecht University under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff, also studying at Leiden. He held the Chair of Sanskrit and taught Indology at Utrecht University from 1929 to 1976.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He served as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Professor of Sinology at the University of Berlin (ca. 1912–1921).
Jan Jaworski worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw from 1923 to 1930 under Stanisław Schayer and also studied under Jean Przyluski.

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University, the Sorbonne, and the University of Berlin, under teachers including Jan Jakob Maria de Groot. He served at Leiden University as a lecturer and later as professor from 1930 to 1954.

Jan N. Bremmer is a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He earned doctorates from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, subsequently holding posts at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and as Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Groningen (1990–2009).

Jan Nattier specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She completed graduate work at Indiana University and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, later holding professorships at Indiana University and Soka University.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper. He also studied under traditional teachers including Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Pieter Hogendijk works in history, archaeology, and mathematics history. He earned his doctorate at Utrecht University and studied under G. J. Toomer, later holding professor posts in the history of mathematics at Leiden University and Utrecht University.

Jan Westerhoff works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge under Michael Potter and another PhD from SOAS, later serving as Lecturer in Philosophy at Durham University and Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at Oxford.

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Leiden University. He held the Chair of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at Leiden (1950–1956) and later served as an editorial consultant at Australian National University.

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under David P. Jackson. He has held positions at the University of Hamburg, the University of Munich, and the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006).
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Surendranath Dasgupta. He held a post attested in 1977 at Jadavpur University.
Janardan Mishra was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Director at the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning, attested in 1959 and 1987.
Jane Bunnag is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD in 1969 from University College London, where she was supervised by E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College and Newnham College, learning under Robert Alexander Neil, and held a post at the University of Cambridge from ca. 1898 to 1922.

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned her BA, MA, and PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. She held posts at Amherst College and became Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 2001.

Janet R. Goodwin is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Delmer M. Brown and held positions at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.
Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Cornell University and earned her PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman, later serving as a professor at Wesleyan University from 1977 to 2013.
